findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: Upon arrival, the only employee who is a certified food protection manager wasn’t present. The cfpm arrived shortly into the visit to correct the violation. The other two owners (married couple), are certified food handlers. Discussed the need of having at least 2 employees manager certified to cover all hours of operation. A website link was provided to the PIC to assist at least one employee with the certified manager’s course in Mandarin.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: There were a couple bins of raw chicken stored above raw beef inside of the walk in cooler. Shown to the PIC and the bins were rearranged to correct the violation. Ensure that raw chicken is always stored beneath any raw beef products to protect against cross contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(2) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (2) Except when combined as ingredients, separating types of raw animal FOODS from each other such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, and POULTRY during storage, preparation, holding, and display by: (a) Using separate EQUIPMENT for each type, or (b) Arranging each type of FOOD in EQUIPMENT so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented, and (c) Preparing each type of FOOD at different times or in separate areas.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: There wasn’t a sanitizer solution created despite the facility being in full operation. A sanitizer solution was created and tested at 100ppm to correct the violation. Ensure that a sani solution is always available if preparing, handling, or serving food.
findings.citation_text: 4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Accumulated food debris was observed on the floors underneath the cookline line. Shown to PIC. Ensure that floors are cleaned as frequent as necessary to prevent debris accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
findings.comment: Observed two cutting boards to be stored behind the faucet of the triple sink. Discussed with PIC and cutting boards were moved to a different location. Ensure that clean equipment is stored in a manner that protects against contamination.
findings.citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Observed at least two employees turn faucet handles off with barehands after the handwashing process. Discussed with PIC proper handwashing techniques. Ensure to use a barrier when turning off faucet handles to prevent recontaminating freshly washed hands. 

2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: Observed facility repurposing bulk peanut container for storage of seasoning (star anise). Facility should cease using allergen containers to hold items not from original package. Switched from peanut container during inspection.

(A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
7-204.11: The bleach available is not an EPA registered product. Replaced with a Chlorox product during inspection. Use Magestic brand for floors, walls, and ceiling. Use approved chemical for sanitizing. 

(A)-(B): Chemical SANITIZERS applied for FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall meet regulatory requirements.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-903.11: Observed a clean cutting board stored behind the faucet of the triple sink. This exposes the clean surface to splash from ware washing and preparation behaviors. Move the cutting board to a clean, dry location where splash is prevented. 


(A) clean FOOD-CONTACT surfaces shall be stored: in clean, dry location, not exposed to splash or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above floor. (B) clean EQUIPMENT shall be stored in self-draining position that allows air drying, covered or inverted. (D) Items that are kept in closed PACKAGES may be stored below 6 inches if on dollies, pallets, racks, and skids properly designed.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-602.13: The facility has a large bowl within a preparation area right by the walk-in cooler. Splash from food preparation has soiled the wall, floor, water heater, and roll cart by this area. Clean the wall, roll cart, and surrounding area by the dry storage so it’s free from food splash. 



 NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
6-403.11: Observed coats stored over dry storage shelving. Provide proper storage for coats and purses so staff doesn’t store personal items on food.

(B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be located in a designated room or area where contamination of FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES cannot occur.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.citation_text:
4-203.11 Metal probe stem thermometer was observed reading around 50F in a pan of diced carrot and celery in the top left compartment of the prep cooler. Inspector’s digital probe thermometer read at 41.5F in the same product, and the cooler was functioning properly at the time of inspection. PIC noted this was a new thermometer just purchased recently. Calibration was discussed. PIC was advised to maintain ice at the facility for calibration of food thermometer that reads 0F-220F. PIC will be asked to demonstrate calibration at next routine inspection.
Food temperature measuring devices that are scaled only in Fahrenheit shall be accurate to ±2F in the intended range of use.

findings.citation_text:

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.citation_text:
2-102.11 (A), (B) & (C)(1), (4)-(16) Priority violations were observed for handwashing, cross contamination, and sanitization. See violations 8, 15, & 16 for details. Facility currently has an active roach population in the compressor compartment of the upright reach-in freezer (next to seafood freezer). See violation 38 for details. findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12 Workers washed hands without proper technique. Manual faucet was shut off without a barrier, and handwashing process was less than 20 seconds. Proper handwashing was discussed. PIC re-educated staff on proper handwashing technique. 
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 Inspector walked in the facility behind two of the workers after they arrived for the day. Hands were not washed upon entering the kitchen. The handwashing sink was blocked and clean equipment was being handled and moved around, including but not limited to, the ice water carafe moved from the walk-in cooler to the lobby and bowls used on the cook line. Handwashing upon arrival and prior to doing any tasks was discussed. PIC advised workers on when to wash hands. 
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands should also be washed when employees arrive to work and enter the kitchen prior to starting any tasks.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:

Handwashing sinks are to be accessible at all times and used only for handwashing.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.citation_text:
6-501.111 Facility currently has an active roach population. Adult and juvenile roaches of various sizes, including a white roach that recently molted, were observed in the compressor compartment of the upright reach-in freezer (next to seafood freezer). Several dead roaches were also observed in the freezer compressor compartment as well as in the compressor compartment of the residential fridge on the cook line. A hatched egg case was also observed in the compressor compartment of the residential fridge. A glue trap containing dead and live roaches was observed under the seafood freezer. Two additional glue traps on the floor behind the grease trap also contained several roaches, and a few dead roaches were observed along the wall under the 3pt sink and the handwashing sink. Cleaning and repairs were discussed. PIC was asked to contact pest control company for service. PIC was advised to request service as soon as possible and let technician know service is needed before the follow-up inspection in two weeks. 
The premises shall be maintained free of pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence by routinely inspecting incoming shipments of food and supplies; routinely inspecting the premises for evidence of pests; using methods, if pests are found, such as trapping devices or other means of pest control as specified under §§ 7-202.12, 7-206.12, and 7-206.13; and eliminating harborage conditions.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12 PIC has a food manager certification that expired in November of 2022. PIC stated they have been busy and unable to find time to re-certify. The importance of certification was discussed as well as options for online and in-person courses. Ensure certification is completed before the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.citation_text:
2-103.11 (O) Two employees working at the time of inspection did not have signed employee health reporting agreements on file. PIC and two other employees had signed reporting agreements available from December 2018. Employee health documents were available in English and provided in Mandarin for employees that needed to review and sign reporting agreements. Ensure all staff are educated on employee health policy upon hiring and sign reporting agreements prior to beginning their first shift. Reporting agreements are needed for all persons working in the facility, even if they are only going to help for a limited amount of time. Maintain signed copies of reporting agreements for staff.
The person in charge shall ensure that food employees are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with law, to the person in charge, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through food, as specified under  2-201.11(A).

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12 Employee was observed wiping hands on a blue towel hanging on dry storage shelving prior to briefly washing their hands at the handwashing sink. Handwashing process took less than 10 seconds, and employee was observed walking away from the handwashing sink with wet hands and no paper towels, which indicated the manual faucet was shut off without a barrier. Proper handwashing procedure and when to wash hands were discussed. Proper use of wiping cloths was also discussed. Ensure wiping cloths are not used to wipe hands and that all staff are properly washing their hands between tasks.
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:

PIC was advised the outer surface of a food package is not considered a clean surface and should not be used to cover foods.  Paper sugar bags were removed and discarded. Plastic wrap was provided to cover tubs of vegetables. 
Food shall only contact equipment and utensils that are cleaned and sanitized as specified in Parts 4-6 and 4-7 of this Code; single-service and single-use articles; and linens, such as cloth napkins, as specified under § 3 304.13 that are laundered as specified under Part 4-8 of this Code.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-302.11 Pan of raw frozen shrimp was observed thawing in a tub on the floor in the walk-in cooler below raw beef and chicken. Raw chicken was also observed over raw beef in the walk-in cooler. Raw animal products were rearranged during inspection to allow for proper storage. Ensure raw animal products are stored properly in the cooler, and store foods up off the floor at least 6 inches. 
Food shall be protected from cross contamination by separating foods from each other such as beef, fish, lamb, pork, and poultry during storage, preparation, holding, and display by arranging each type of food in equipment so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 (A)(2) Cooked lo mein noodles in the bottom of the prep cooler were observed with a surface temperature of 48F-50F and an internal temperature of 56F-58F. Noodles were said to be in and out of the cooler during lunch service. Noodles were discarded. The use of time control for a working supply of noodles during busy periods was discussed. 
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.citation_text:
3-501.15 Eggrolls and fried chicken pieces were observed cooling at room temperature. Products were said to be cooked within the last 30 to 35 minutes prior to inspector’s arrival. Internal temperatures ranged from 79F to 105F for eggrolls and 91F-127F for chicken. A portion of fried chicken still at the wok had an internal temperature ranging from 99F to 133F at the bottom where product was near heat source. Best practices were discussed, as well as monitoring time and temperature during the cooling process. All foods were placed in the walk-in cooler to finish rapid chilling. 
Cooling shall be accomplished in accordance with the following time and temperature criteria: 135F to 70F/below in 2hrs and 70F to 41F/below in additional 4hrs (total cooling time must not exceed 6hrs). One or more of the following methods shall be used to cool foods based on the type of food being cooled: (1)place food in shallow pans; (2) separate food into smaller or thinner portions; (3) use rapid cooling equipment; (4) stir food in a container placed in an ice water bath; (5) use containers that facilitate heat transfer; (6) add ice as an ingredient (when applicable); and/or (7) other effective methods. When placed in cooling or cold holding equipment, food containers in which food is being cooled shall be arranged to provide maximum heat transfer through the container walls and loosely covered, or uncovered if protected from overhead contamination during the cooling period to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625  Sec. 3.06 Facility was not in compliance with food handler law. Two employees have food handler certifications that expired in 2020, and two other employees have not competed a food handler course. Ensure all staff that are not certified food managers complete an online food handler certification course within 30 days of hiring and that re-certification occurs prior to expiration dates. Maintain copies of current certifications on-site. 
All food handlers, other than someone who has a food manager certification, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 Sec. 3.07 PIC has an allergen certification that expired in 2021. Ensure re-certification occurs before the next routine inspection. 
Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.comment:
3-501.13: Observed chopped steak to be thawing in the 3 part sink without running water over it. Ensure there is running water over the foods when thawing to prevent bacteria accumulation in the food. The faucet was turned on during the inpsection to correct the violation. 
TCS FOOD shall be thawed: (A) at 41F or below in refrigeration (B) completely submerged under running water, not getting above 41F (water temp of 70F or below). If food will be cooked, not getting above 41F for more than 4 hours. (C) part of the cooking process (D) Using any procedure if RTE FOOD is thawed and prepared for immediate service (E) ROP FISH that bear label shall be removed from packaging before thawing under refrigeration, upon completion of thawing from running water.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.citation_text: 7-204.11  (P) The bleach being used as a sanitizer did not have an EPA registration number. Chemical Bleach when used as a sanitizer on food contact surfaces must have an EPA registration number on the label and instructions for use in kitchens or food contact surfaces.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment: Observed raw shell eggs stored above vegetables in the walk in cooler. Store all raw animal products below ready to eat foods. Eggs were moved to the raw animal product area and stored above the raw chicken. 3-302.11  (P)  Store ready to eat foods above raw foods to protect from cross-contamination. Reference 3-302.11.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment: Observed two large tubs of chicken stored in ambient air that were reported to have been cooked approximately 2 hours ago to be probed at 109F. Heaping pans of egg rolls stored in ambient air on the speed rack were also observed to be probed at 110F--these were reported to have been made 1 hour ago. No cooling logs are available at the time of the inspection. Given that the final cooking temperature of these items is typically 180-200F, a portion of the time these have spent in ambient air the items would have been well above hot holding temperatures; therefore, chicken was transferred to pans and placed more in single layers and taken to the walk in cooler. Eggs rolls will be arranged and placed in the freezer to finish cooling. It is evident that rapid cooling is not occurring today. Cooling must occur rapidly so that foods cool from 135F to 70F within 2 hours and then from 70F to 41F or below within an additional 4 hours.  3-501.15  (Pf) The method of cooling is inadequate. Use one or more of the following methods based on the type of food being cooled: placing the food in shallow pans; separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; using containers that facilitate heat transfer; adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Discussed HACCP concept with the person in charge. Reference 3-501.15.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment: Wet wiping cloth was observed sitting on the top of the prep table. Store wet wiping cloths in sanitizer solution in between use. Cloth was placed in sanitizer. 3-304.14  (C) In-use wiping cloths are not stored properly. Cloths used for wiping spills shall be maintained dry. Cloths used to wipe surfaces and equipment shall be held in proper sanitizer solution. Cloths in-use for wiping surfaces in contact with raw animalfoods shall be kept separate from cloths used for other purposes. In-use cloths must be laundered daily. Reference 3-304.14.
